description: It’s time to rethink welfare as AI reshapes the economy and wears down the brains of some of the most vulnerable workers AI is adding to the cognitive load of workers already stretched thin by unpredictable pay, insecure housing and mounting debt – and the lowest paid feel it most. We need to rethink welfare for an economy being reshaped by AI. Throughout the history of the study of economics, the human brain, which directs our labour, judgment and resilience, has rarely been considered an asset in its own right. The emerging AI economy is changing that. As machines take on routine work, what becomes most valuable is the judgment, creativity and insights only people can provide. Economists coined a term for this in recent years: brain capital. You know the ones, the pavement-blocking LED monoliths, with screens on both sides broadcasting six ads per minute to passersby. Even as shops have shuttered, numbers of such ad machines skyrocketed 256% between 2018 and 2025. The ads shown are invariably for global mega-corporations, further driving commerce online, and for unhealthy products such as junk food, alcohol, gambling and vapes (although the latter are to be banned from 1 June 2027). description: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — NASA’s Voyager 1 has phoned home from one light-day away , humanity’s first emissary to cross this monumental threshold way out in interstellar space . That’s how long it took for the radio signal to traverse the more than 16 billion miles (26 billion kilometers) at the speed of light. “Voyager 1 light-day distance confirmed ...
